title: Sebastian and the Border
premise: Petra Thornbury, a crash investigator haunted by the unexplained deaths in row twelve, receives a meeting invitation from a handler she buried three years ago. Following it, she uncovers evidence that the crash was engineered to silence a witness to a cross-border arms deal protected by three governments. Hunted by an assassin who once saved her life, Petra must smuggle the truth to a dying whistleblower's daughter while deciding whether justice can exist outside the law. In the end, she trades her own anonymity for exposure, releasing the evidence publicly and forcing a reckoning she may not survive.
about_author: Edmund Amberdale is the pen name of a former aviation-adjacent civil servant who spent a decade inside institutions he no longer trusts. He writes thrillers about ordinary professionals trapped between procedure and conscience.

chapters.title: Row Twelve
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Three years after the crash that killed her family, Petra works cold cases at the Transport Safety Bureau, still quietly re-examining the row twelve anomaly. She receives a calendar invitation from her dead handler, Marcus Hale, scheduled for tomorrow. Emotional beat: grief cracked open by the impossible.

chapters.title: The Invitation
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. She verifies the invitation's metadata and finds it routed through a decommissioned government server only Hale used. Colleagues notice her distraction; her supervisor, Voss, offers a suspicious transfer. Beat: paranoia taking root as routine begins to feel like a cage.

chapters.title: Meeting the Dead
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. At an abandoned rail depot, she finds not Hale but a dead-drop: his old notebook and a drive containing flight data proving the crash's transponder was spoofed. A watcher in the distance. Beat: dread and exhilaration colliding as grief becomes evidence.

chapters.title: The Assassin's Ledger
chapters.summary: Ilse Kovač's POV. The assassin known as Meridian reviews a contract on 'the Thornbury woman' and recognizes her as the civilian she once shielded during an operation gone wrong. She requests 48 hours before acting. Beat: cold professionalism shadowed by an old debt.

chapters.title: Rules Rewritten
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Petra cross-checks the flight data against sealed reports and finds three versions of the same night, each edited by a different agency. Voss warns her to stop digging; her clearance is quietly revoked. Beat: betrayal by the institution she served.

chapters.title: Hale's Ghost
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Following notebook clues, Petra locates Hale's safehouse and finds signs he lived there for months after his 'death' — and a second drive addressed to 'the daughter.' A break-in suggests she's not the only one hunting. Beat: hope that Hale may still be alive.

chapters.title: The Daughter
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. In Rotterdam, Petra finds Ana Hale, a customs analyst who never knew her father's real work. Ana reveals Marcus contacted her a week ago — before Petra got her invitation. Beat: the timeline fractures; someone is impersonating the dead.

chapters.title: Three Governments
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. The drives point to Operation LATTICE: an arms corridor protected by officials in three countries, with the crash staged to eliminate a witness. Petra realizes the truth must go public because no single agency can be trusted. Beat: resolve hardening into mission.

chapters.title: Meridian Closes
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Ilse tracks Petra to Rotterdam but finds a rival contractor already on-site. She kills him in a stairwell and warns Petra with a single note: 'They sent two. I'm the slower one.' Beat: uneasy alliance offered from the barrel of a gun.

chapters.title: Safehouse Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Petra and Ana hide in a canal house, decrypting the second drive: live bank routing for LATTICE's payments. Petra teaches Ana tradecraft while wrestling with using a child of the conspiracy as a courier. Beat: found family under siege.

chapters.title: The Journalist's Price
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Petra approaches disgraced investigative reporter Declan Okafor, who agrees to publish — if she gives him everything, including her own Bureau file. Voss surfaces in his notes as a source years ago. Beat: trust as a calculated gamble.

chapters.title: Interception
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Ilse intercepts a LATTICE courier and learns the third drive — the one naming all three governments' signatories — never existed; Hale split it into people, not files. Ana is the final key. Beat: the hunt reframes around the girl.

chapters.title: Voss
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Petra confronts Voss in Brussels; he admits he rewrote the reports under orders but claims Hale was the architect of LATTICE's exposure plan — and its casualty. He offers immunity for the drives. Beat: the mentor's face finally matching the mask.

chapters.title: What Hale Buried
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Decoding Hale's notebook fully, Petra finds his confession: he faked his death to finish the work, and the invitation was a dead-man's switch timed to her grief. He is alive — and dying. Beat: fury and forgiveness fighting for the same ground.

chapters.title: The Slow Assassin
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Ilse burns her handler network to buy Petra time, knowing it signs her own death warrant. She meets Petra and hands over the contractor kill-list. Beat: loyalty redefined as choosing a side at personal ruin.

chapters.title: Border Crossing
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Smuggling Ana and the evidence across the German-Polish border during a freight transfer, Petra uses crash-investigation protocols to spoof a customs scan. They are nearly caught by a LATTICE mole inside border police. Beat: competence as survival, terror held at bay by procedure.

chapters.title: Hale, Alive
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. In a hospice outside Gdańsk, Petra faces Hale, emaciated and lucid. He explains row twelve: her family's seats were collateral of the targeting error he tried to prevent. He asks her to decide — bury it or burn it. Beat: the confrontation with the man who cost her everything.

chapters.title: The Choice
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Petra weighs Hale's plea for a controlled, legal disclosure against the certainty that LATTICE will bury it. Ana, who has read everything, tells her the dead in row twelve deserve the whole truth, not a redacted version. Beat: the thematic fulcrum — loyalty to people versus truth itself.

chapters.title: Burning LATTICE
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Petra gives Okafor the full archive and schedules simultaneous release across three jurisdictions. LATTICE retaliates: Okafor's office is raided, Ana is taken, and the assassin sent for Petra is not Ilse. Beat: the plan detonating early.

chapters.title: The Exchange
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Ilse trades herself to LATTICE's brokers to learn Ana's location, then goes off-ledger one last time. Petra and Ilse extract Ana from a black-site annex in a violent, costly raid. Beat: justice outside the law, paid for in blood.

chapters.title: Publication Day
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. The story breaks worldwide; signatories fall, Voss testifies, and Hale dies within hours of the headlines, his name cleared and damned at once. Petra surrenders to investigators on her own terms. Beat: catharsis with a bill attached.

chapters.title: After the Border
chapters.summary: Petra's POV, coda. Six months later, Petra testifies at the tribunal, visits a new memorial with row twelve finally explained, and takes tea with Ana, now in witness care. Ilse's fate remains an open file. Beat: quiet, earned peace — identity rebuilt on truth instead of grief.
